commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[eval] Normalize and catalog rollout conversations (#9236)

Write Evalchemy and Harbor conversations to a shared FineStore
`rollouts_v1` table keyed by evaluation identity, turn, and content
part. The schema distinguishes completion, chat, and agentic
conversations; normalizes participant and content roles; and retains
Harbor token counts, token IDs, log probabilities, and costs.

Marin derives rollout rows from evaluator-owned `samples` and `steps`
after those tables are sealed. The completion object is bound to their
source-table snapshot, so successful retries are no-ops while resumed
runs with new source rows are normalized again. Physical rollout tables
are schema-versioned. Existing sample and step tables, raw evaluator
source artifacts, and trajectory blobs are unchanged; no Evalchemy or
Harbor upstream change is required.

Register terminal evaluation and SkyRL attempts in Finelog
`marin.rollout_runs`. Eval rows point to their FineStore archive, while
SkyRL rows point to the retained trajectory directory and terminal
manifest, making rollout-producing runs discoverable without duplicating
their payloads in Finelog.

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Use scheduler preemption for CoreWeave verification (#9234)

Allow `iris-batch` Pods to preempt lower-priority Kubernetes Pods and
remove Iris’s cross-namespace verification eviction loop. CoreWeave
verification Pods bypass Kueue with the unconstrained-topology
annotation, so Kueue can admit Iris workloads and kube-scheduler selects
only the priority `-1` verification Pods needed for placement.

A live single-node check on `cw-us-east-02a` admitted an 8-GPU Kueue
Workload over an annotated verification Pod; kube-scheduler preempted
the test and scheduled the workload three seconds later.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Coordinate hero garbage collection at shared steps (#9224)

Add opt-in coordinated cyclic garbage collection to the hero EP training
loop through `--gc-interval 100` in the diagnostics launcher or
`hero_grug_trainer_config(gc_interval=100)`. After ten local warmup
updates, disable automatic cyclic collection and collect once;
thereafter a training hook collects at completed global steps divisible
by the interval and on normal training completion. Scheduled collection
runs before checkpoint decisions. Evaluation wrappers also collect after
each evaluation returns. The shared step cadence coordinates collection;
GC adds no barriers. Restore the previous GC policy on normal or
exceptional exit. Coordinated GC remains disabled by default. Local GC,
checkpoint, and full-iteration timings and a GC profiler annotation
expose the resulting cost.

The hero planning estimate is roughly 0.6 seconds less amortized time
per update, or 3–4%, if coordination removes most of the observed
staggered-GC overhead. The [production
diagnosis](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/455) attributed 3.83% of
eligible elapsed time to excess above a quiet-step baseline: about 0.675
seconds of the 17.591-second mean update. A shared 1.5-second collection
every 100 updates would cost about 0.015 seconds/update, leaving a
conditional estimate of 0.66 seconds saved. The residual also includes
other delays, and the slowest collection across 704 ranks is unmeasured,
so this is a planning estimate rather than a measured hero speedup.

The [64-GPU
validation](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Fgc-sync-9205-hook-20260917-coord)
used the full model with one sequence per GPU, ten warmup updates, and
300 measured updates per arm. Elapsed time including the treatment’s
initial and final collections fell from 795.576 to 776.003 seconds
(2.46%; 2.652 to 2.587 seconds/update). Before the final callback pass,
elapsed time fell from 795.575 to 774.700 seconds (2.62%). Automatic GC
produced 72 full collections across 48 steps; coordinated GC produced
one collection per rank after warmup, at global updates 100/200/300, and
on normal completion at global update 310. Scheduled collections ran
through the training hook before checkpoint decisions. The slowest
rank’s periodic collections took 1.15–1.22 seconds; final collection
took up to 1.30 seconds.

Both arms had identical sampled live HBM (35.094 GiB per rank) and
allocator peaks (111.840 GiB), with no increase above their post-warmup
baselines. Live memory was sampled every ten measured steps and at
completion; the allocator peak includes warmup. Maximum sampled
treatment RSS growth was 54.4 MiB per rank above the post-warmup
baseline. This single pair exercised checkpoint decisions with writes
and evaluation disabled. Production-batch throughput, evaluation
transitions, and long-term memory behavior still need a monitored
production trial; the production hero is not enabled by this change.

Part of #9205.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Add a --seed override to the eval launcher (#9221)

The eval launcher took its sampling seed only from the Evalchemy config
file,
so repeating an eval across seeds (for example AIME24's ten seeded runs)
meant
one YAML variant per seed or identical launches. `launch --seed N`
overrides
the seed of every Evalchemy definition in the launch, and the override
reaches
each run record's evalchemy.seed so differently seeded launches keep
distinct
provenance. Harbor definitions are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
Raise direct inference timeouts to 12 hours (#9226)

Raise the default request timeout from 35 minutes to 12 hours for both
the Iris proxy and the dashboard's upstream HTTP client. Non-streaming
AIME evaluations at 64K tokens hit the old deadline while vLLM was still
generating; at the observed roughly 49 ms per token, a full response
would take about 53 minutes.

At that rate, 262K tokens would take about 3.6 hours. The 12-hour limit
leaves headroom for slower decoding and request queueing, while staying
below the eval client's 24-hour timeout. Existing deployments must be
relaunched to pick up the new default.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <bf996@nyu.edu>

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Add W&B run forking (#9231)

Expose W&B run forking through `WandbConfig`. A fork creates a distinct
child
run from a selected parent-history step. A later recovery launch reuses
the
child ID without `fork_from`.

W&B forbids `resume` and `fork_from` together, so fork initialization
omits
`resume`. The configuration validates the handoff format and rejects a
child
run that names itself as its source.

Part of #8506

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[eval] Store evaluator output directly in FineStore (#9177)

Route evaluator output through FineStore at the producer boundary.
Evalchemy stores its native results JSON and per-task sample JSONL as
source artifacts and writes normalized sample rows. Harbor stores typed
trial results, trajectories, and job config, lock, and result files as
source artifacts and writes normalized samples and trajectory steps.
FineStore owns generic artifact storage and the shared schemas; it
contains no evaluator-specific conversion.

Marin now passes the archive destination to each evaluator and reads the
resulting records.

An Iceball Micro run on `cw-us-east-08a` completed both evaluators:
Evalchemy wrote 256 GSM8K rows for 128 documents across two extraction
filters plus its native source artifacts; Harbor wrote two AIME sample
rows plus its job and trial artifacts. A final Evalchemy run against the
merged producer pin completed in 4 minutes 59 seconds, and an
independent read-back found 256 rows under `gsm8k_5shot` with both
native source artifacts present.

Detailed ownership and live-run evidence:
https://loom.oa.dev/s/4d4aj9d9/artifacts/finestore-native-evaluation-delivery

---------

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Avoid deletes when committing remote checkpoint metadata (#9215)

Commit remote checkpoint metadata directly to its final object after
tensor serialization completes. Remote object writers publish on close,
so metadata remains the completion marker without a sibling
copy-and-delete. Local filesystems keep the atomic sibling rename.

PR #8974 changed checkpoint metadata publication from a direct write to
a sibling rename, introducing a delete operation under the permanent
checkpoint prefix. The CoreWeave policy denies deletion under permanent
hero checkpoint prefixes. The previous remote rename copied
`metadata.json` into place and then failed to delete its temporary
source. The asynchronous `AccessDenied` surfaced at the next checkpoint
and ended the training attempt. Regression coverage checks publication
with deletion denied and propagation of a close-time publication failure
without a discoverable completion marker.

Incident: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/459

Coordinator lock-release deletion is a separate follow-up. Its retained
failures occur when the coordinator exits its orchestration step;
heartbeat refresh and stale-lock takeover use writes. It can obscure
shutdown errors and leave a lease until it expires, but it is not
required for this metadata fix and is not known to interrupt the ongoing
training loop.

---------

commits.message:
[grug] Skip padded tokens in MoE dispatch (#9159)

Exclude attention-mask padding from routed MoE dispatch, logical
capacity, routing statistics, and QB threshold updates. Static
collective and receiver-buffer shapes remain unchanged, while invalid
assignments consume no logical capacity or expert gradient and are
reported separately from sender and receiver drops.

Padded inputs match their compact equivalents for valid-token outputs
and gradients, including capacity overflow and four-device execution
with an all-padding shard. The affected safe suite passed 725 tests, and
the focused MoE and model suite passed 127 tests. Accelerator-only
ragged and DeepEP execution remains hardware-gated. The fresh-process
benchmark reports forward and backward runtime and allocator peak deltas
for representative accelerator shapes.

Fixes #8953

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[grafana] Separate Finelog outages from invalid alert results (#9152)

Return schema-valid zero rows for training and Zephyr alerts, and no
data for storage alerts whose no-data state is OK, when Finelog reports
a retryable RPC, transport, or discovery failure.
`FinelogFleetUnhealthy` continues to report the outage.

Keep every Grafana rule's execution-error state at Alerting. Invalid
queries, missing namespaces, oversized results, invalid Arrow payloads,
and alert projection errors remain visible as execution errors.

During a Finelog hub restart on 2026-09-14, retryable failures reached
Grafana, whose Alerting execution-error state converted them into firing
alert instances. The new alert endpoints consume only typed
unavailability before Grafana evaluates the result. The fleet monitor
already covers that failure: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/433

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaluation] Read the standard error of Evalchemy repeated-sample tasks (#9196)

Quick summary:

Evalchemy and lm-eval reported stderr statistics with a slightly
different name convention, and our stats reader didn't account for this.
As a result, some evals in evalchemy like AIME24 would have no visible
stderr and result in an interval of 0-1. This fixes that.



Agent speak:

Evalchemy's aime24 task averages over repeats and writes the mean as
`accuracy_avg` with its standard error as `accuracy_std_err`. The record
reader only knew lm-eval's `<metric>_stderr` spelling, so every aime24
measurement carried no dispersion and an interval of [0, 1]. The panel
sorts a benchmark column on the interval lower bound, so every model
tied at 0.0 and clicking the AIME24 header changed nothing in either
direction. The same tie hid the ranking in Compare and in the Δ-best
column.

`stderr_for` now pairs `<metric>_avg` with `<metric>_std_err`, and
`primary_metric` no longer treats `accuracy_std_err` as a headline
candidate. The measurement stays continuous: the repeats are re-runs of
the same 30 items, not independent items, so the recorded standard error
across repeats is the right dispersion and a Wilson interval over 300
trials would be too narrow.

On the production record `20260721-003923-qwen3-1.7b-aime24-3d7f`
(accuracy_avg 0.163, accuracy_std_err 0.0173) the interval moves from
[0.000, 1.000] to [0.129, 0.197]. Existing records need no rewrite; the
reader is the one place that knows a harness's metric spelling. The
evaldash fixtures gain an aime24 record for snowball and tootsie-8b in
the Evalchemy spelling, so the local dashboard shows the interval and a
fixture test guards it. The Harbor aime runs with `pass@1` and
`n_scored: 0` are a separate data problem and are not changed here.

Found while checking the sort direction toggle from #9104.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Sort panel benchmark columns on the score (#9198)

Before:
A panel benchmark column sorted on the interval lower bound after
https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8122 . Any column whose
intervals are wide or degenerate then ties every row at the same bound,
and the header toggle changes nothing. AIME24 showed this: every cell
read 0.0-100.0 (#9196 fixes the missing dispersion behind that), so
clicking the header in either direction left the rows in name order.

Now:
The panel now orders a benchmark column by the score itself, which is
what the cell shows in large type. The fleet-best marker and the
delta-best figure pick the column leader by the same rule, with the
lower bound as the tie-break

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[nightshift] fix documentation drift (#9132)

> Seed hums, digits drift —
> the doc still names a river
> the code rerouted.

`docs/design/finelog-exact-analytics.md` describes Finelog's segment
index
family in the present tense, and the implementation moved past it.

The `IndexSpec` enum listed four variants; it now has six. Document
`AdaptiveValueCounts` and `AdaptiveGroupExtrema`, their query families,
and the
`Schema.grouped_extrema` declaration that drives the second one.
Adaptive
sections are best-effort: a segment that declines one above its
cardinality or
byte budget stays complete, while a missing declared `ValueCounts`
section still
makes the bundle stale.

Value-count substitution no longer requires complete coverage across
visible
segments. Contained segments read summaries, boundary and L0 segments
keep an
ordinary aggregate, and a final aggregate merges both exactly; grouped
extrema
use the same shape under `FinelogGroupExtrema`.

Correct the `training-status` projection column list, which was missing
`run_id`, `job_id`, and `attributes_json`, and record that the telemetry
schema
now declares fourteen projections rather than one. Mark the benchmark
section as
the acceptance run for the original four-method family so its numbers
are not
read as current.

The other five docs under `docs/design/` were checked against the code
in the
same pass. Their file paths, symbols, and config values still resolve,
and the
markdown links are intact.

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Cut duplicated packing, HTML parsing, and profile-duration code paths (#9223)

Three independent cleanups, one per subproject.

`levanter/data/packing.py` carried two packing implementations. Nothing
calls
`SequencePacker` or `pack_prompt_completions`: eval_harness packs
through
`greedy_pack_prompt_completions`/`pack_documents`, and only the tests
kept the
pool-based path alive. Removing it drops 276 lines, including the module
docstring that still described the pool strategy rather than the greedy
one in
use. `test_per_segment_loss` built its packed example with
`SequencePacker`, so
it now constructs the `LmExample` directly with the same segment layout,
the way
the neighboring `test_segment_correct` does.

`clean_wiki_html` chained three helpers that each parsed the HTML string
into
their own BeautifulSoup tree and serialized it back, so every article in
a
multi-million-article Wikipedia dump paid three parse and serialize
round trips
where one suffices. The helpers now mutate a shared soup that
`clean_wiki_html`
parses and serializes once, matching how the sibling ar5iv transform
composes
its cleanup steps. `html.parser` is not idempotent over its own output,
so head
`<link>`/`<meta>` elements now serialize without the synthetic
self-closing slash
and pick up a stray closing tag; Resiliparse re-parses the result
downstream and
treats them as void either way, and the extracted markdown is
byte-identical
across all nine Wikipedia snapshot fixtures.

Iris resolved the wire default for an unset
`ProfileTaskRequest.duration_seconds`
at four sites: the controller sized its forwarding RPC timeout from a
private
copy, the federation peer sized the parent->peer proxy budget from a
second copy,
the k8s backend resolved a bare `or 10` at capture time, and the worker
fell back
to a constructor default. The controller forwards the unset field
verbatim, so
raising one literal alone leaves the capture running past the budget of
the hop
waiting for it. `DEFAULT_PROFILE_DURATION_SECONDS` now lives in
`cluster.runtime.profile`, the module that already owns the capture
helpers all
four callers import. Behavior is unchanged.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Enforce benchmark metric and coverage protocols (#9145)

Evaldash previously inferred a task's headline metric and treated the
number of scored samples as enough to judge whether a run covered its
benchmark. That let small capped runs replace complete results and made
tasks such as DROP report a different metric from the evaluator's
intended score.

Evaluation harnesses now emit a versioned benchmark protocol with
canonical metric names, uncertainty kinds, and full and attempted item
counts. Marin stores that metadata and the harness's canonical results
in `record.json`, uses them for coverage admission and column
comparisons, and keeps source metrics for provenance. Evalchemy supplies
per-task protocols for lm-eval and chat-native tasks. Harbor reports
continuous reward with the standard error across scored trials and
scales task counts by the configured trials per task.

Records without evaluator metadata continue through the legacy reader.
Known historical aliases map to their canonical names so existing
columns remain populated while benchmarks are rerun. Runs with
undeclared custom tasks remain readable alongside declared tasks.

Validated with the required lint, 395 affected tests (1 skipped), 137
focused producer and reader tests, the Evaldash production build, and a
real Harbor metadata preflight. The Evalchemy cluster smoke launch could
not submit because the configured application-default credentials file
is absent in this environment.

Fixes #8148
Fixes #8144

commits.author: jyizheng
commits.message:
[levanter] Clamp untuned fused-CE block sizes to the weight-tile budget (#8932)

On Hopper the fused cross-entropy autotune swept its block-size
candidates on every call. The cache key requires tracing the kernel with
the inferred block sizes; for shapes with no tuned entry, inference
returns the default BlockSizes (h=512, v=1024), whose weight tile
exceeds the NVIDIA shared-memory budget that
`_validate_launch_feasibility` enforces. The trace raises, so the sweep
result is never retained. Move the budget into config.py, shared by the
launch check and inference, and clamp the untuned default by halving v
then h until it fits. Tuned entries and non-NVIDIA devices are
unchanged.

Fixes #8853

Co-authored-by: David Hall <david.hall@openathena.ai>
